claim: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval gives milliseconds access with the same throughput as S3 Standard and S3 Standard-IA; unlike Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive, no Restore request is needed.
question: Do you need a Restore request to read an S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval object?

values.display: do not need to issue a Restore request

evidence.quote: Unlike the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage classes, which are designed for asynchronous access, you do not need to issue a Restore request before accessing an object stored in S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval.

claim: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is ideal for data accessed about once a quarter that still needs milliseconds retrieval, with a lower storage price and slightly higher access costs than S3 Standard-IA.
question: When is S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval the right class?

evidence.quote: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is ideal if you have data that is rarely accessed (once a quarter) and requires milliseconds retrieval times. It’s the ideal storage class if you want the same low latency and high throughput performance as S3 Standard-IA, but store data that is accessed less frequently than S3 Standard-IA, with a lower storage price and slightly higher data access costs.

claim: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval objects have a minimum of 90 days of storage; an object deleted, overwritten or transitioned before 90 days incurs a pro-rated charge for the remaining days.
question: What is the minimum storage duration for S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval?

qualifiers.scope: per object, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval

evidence.quote: Objects that are archived to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval have a minimum of 90 days of storage, and objects deleted, overwritten, or transitioned before 90 days incur a pro-rated charge equal to the storage charge for the remaining days.

claim: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval has a minimum object storage charge of 128KB.
question: What is the minimum billable object size in S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval?

qualifiers.scope: per object, S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval

evidence.quote: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is designed for larger objects and has a minimum object storage charge of 128KB. Objects smaller than 128KB in size will incur storage charges as if the object were 128KB.

claim: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is designed for 99.9% availability, the same as S3 Standard-IA, with service credits if availability is less than 99% in a billing cycle.
question: What availability is S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval designed for, and when do credits apply?

evidence.quote: S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval is designed for 99.999999999% (11 9s) of durability and 99.9% availability, the same as S3 Standard-IA, and carries a service level agreement providing service credits if availability is less than 99% in any billing cycle.

claim: From S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval, Expedited retrievals are typically available within 1-5 minutes, Standard retrievals complete in 3-5 hours, and Bulk retrievals complete within 5-12 hours and are free.
question: How long do Expedited, Standard and Bulk retrievals take from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval?

evidence.quote: For all but the largest objects (250MB+), data accessed using Expedited retrievals are typically made available within 1-5 minutes. Objects retrieved using Standard retrievals typically complete between 3-5 hours. Standard retrievals typically start in minutes when initiated using S3 Batch Operations. Bulk retrievals typically complete within 5—12 hours, and are free of charge.

claim: Without provisioned capacity, Expedited retrievals might not be accepted during periods of high demand.
question: Are Expedited retrievals guaranteed without provisioned capacity?

evidence.quote: Without provisioned capacity, expedited retrievals might not be accepted during periods of high demand.

claim: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval objects have a minimum of 90 days of storage; earlier deletion, overwrite or transition incurs a pro-rated charge for the remaining days.
question: What is the minimum storage duration for S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval?

qualifiers.scope: per object, S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval

evidence.quote: Objects archived to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval have a minimum of 90 days of storage. If an object is deleted, overwritten, or transitioned before 90 days, a pro-rated charge equal to the storage charge for the remaining days will be incurred.

claim: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval adds 40 KB of metadata per archived object: 32 KB billed at the Glacier rate and 8 KB billed at the S3 Standard rate.
question: How much metadata overhead does each archived object add in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval?

evidence.quote: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval also requires 40 KB of additional metadata for each archived object. This includes 32 KB of metadata charged at the S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval rate required to identify and retrieve your data. And, an additional 8 KB data charged at the S3 Standard rate which is required to maintain the user-defined name and metadata for objects archived to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.

claim: A retrieval from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval creates a temporary copy in S3 Standard for the number of days you specify, and leaves the archived data intact.
question: What does a restore from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval create?

evidence.quote: The retrieval request creates a temporary copy of your data in the S3 Standard storage class while leaving the archived data intact in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. You can specify the amount of time in days for which the temporary copy is stored in Amazon S3.

claim: S3 Event Notifications can tell you when an object has been restored from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and its temporary copy is available.
question: How do you find out that a Glacier restore has finished?

evidence.quote: With restore notifications, you can now be notified with an S3 Event Notification when an object has successfully restored from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and the temporary copy is made available to you.

claim: Expedited and Standard retrievals have a per-GB retrieval fee and a per-request fee; Bulk retrievals from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval are free.
question: Which S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval option has no retrieval fee?

values.display: Bulk Retrievals from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval are free

evidence.quote: Expedited and Standard have a per-GB retrieval fee and per-request fee (i.e., you pay for requests made against your Amazon S3 objects). Bulk Retrievals from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval are free.

claim: S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval costs up to 10% less than S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, for archive data accessed 1-2 times per year and retrieved asynchronously.
question: How much cheaper is Flexible Retrieval than Instant Retrieval, and for what access pattern?

evidence.quote: The S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval storage class delivers low-cost storage, up to 10% lower cost (than S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval), for archive data that is accessed 1-2 times per year and is retrieved asynchronously, with free bulk retrievals.

claim: You can PUT directly into S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval by specifying GLACIER in the x-amz-storage-class header, or transition objects from any active-data class with Lifecycle rules.
question: How does data get into S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval?

evidence.quote: You can directly PUT into S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval by specifying GLACIER in the x-amz-storage-class header. You can also use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from any of the S3 storage classes for active data (S3 Standard, S3 Intelligent-Tiering, S3 Standard-IA, S3 One Zone-IA, and S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval) to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval based on object age.

claim: S3 Glacier Deep Archive starts from $0.00099 per GB-month, about $1 per TB-month, for data accessed once or twice a year.
question: What does S3 Glacier Deep Archive cost per GB-month?

qualifiers.scope: S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage, lowest Region price

evidence.quote: From just $0.00099 per GB-month (less than one-tenth of one cent, or about $1 per TB-month), S3 Glacier Deep Archive offers the lowest cost storage in the cloud, at prices significantly lower than storing and maintaining data in on-premises magnetic tape libraries or archiving data off-site.

claim: Deep Archive Standard retrieval (the default) returns data within 12 hours, typically starting within 9 hours with S3 Batch Operations; Bulk retrieval typically completes within 48 hours.
question: How long does a restore from S3 Glacier Deep Archive take?

evidence.quote: Standard is the default tier and lets you access any of your archived objects within 12 hours, with retrievals typically starting within 9 hours when initiated using S3 Batch Operations. Bulk lets you retrieve large amounts of data, even petabytes of data, inexpensively and typically completes within 48 hours.

claim: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is up to 75% less expensive than S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval.
question: How much cheaper is Deep Archive than Flexible Retrieval?

values.spoken: up to seventy-five percent less expensive

evidence.quote: S3 Glacier Deep Archive is up to 75% less expensive than S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and provides retrieval within 12 hours using the Standard retrieval tier.

claim: S3 Glacier Deep Archive objects have a minimum of 180 days of storage; earlier deletion, overwrite or transition incurs a pro-rated charge for the remaining days.
question: What is the minimum storage duration for S3 Glacier Deep Archive?

qualifiers.scope: per object, S3 Glacier Deep Archive

evidence.quote: Objects that are archived to S3 Glacier Deep Archive have a minimum of 180 days of storage. If an object is deleted, overwritten, or transitioned before 180 days, a pro-rated charge equal to the storage charge for the remaining days will be incurred.

claim: To move tape archives into S3 Glacier Deep Archive, AWS suggests Tape Gateway (a virtual tape library for existing backup applications), AWS Snowball for terabytes to petabytes, or AWS Direct Connect.
question: How does AWS recommend migrating tape archives to S3 Glacier Deep Archive?

evidence.quote: You can use the AWS Tape Gateway to integrate with existing backup applications using a virtual tape library (VTL) interface. This interface presents virtual tapes to the backup application.
You can also use AWS Snowball to migrate data. Snowball accelerates moving terabytes to petabytes of data into and out of AWS using physical storage devices designed to be secure for transport.
Finally, you can use AWS Direct Connect to establish dedicated network connections from your premises to AWS.

claim: S3 Glacier Deep Archive appears as its own service line item on the AWS bill, separate from S3, but Cost Management reports include it under Amazon S3.
question: Where does S3 Glacier Deep Archive usage appear on the bill?

evidence.quote: S3 Glacier Deep Archive usage and cost will show up as an independent service line item on your monthly AWS bill, separate from your Amazon S3 usage and costs.

claim: There is no cost to set up Lifecycle policies; a transition request is charged per object when the object becomes eligible for transition.
question: What does S3 Lifecycle cost?

evidence.quote: There is no additional cost to set up and apply Lifecycle policies. A transition request is charged per object when an object becomes eligible for transition according to the Lifecycle rule.

claim: A Lifecycle rule that expires incomplete multipart uploads removes the uncommitted parts and their storage after a set number of days, so you stop paying for parts that were never completed.
question: Why expire incomplete multipart uploads with a Lifecycle rule?

evidence.quote: For example, if your application uploads several multipart object parts, but never commits them, you will still be charged for that storage. This policy can lower your S3 storage bill by automatically removing incomplete multipart uploads and the associated storage after a predefined number of days.

claim: Lifecycle policies apply to both existing and new objects in the bucket.
question: Does a new Lifecycle rule affect objects that already exist?

values.display: both existing and new S3 objects

evidence.quote: S3 Lifecycle policies apply to both existing and new S3 objects, helping you optimize storage and maximize cost savings for all current data and any new data placed in S3 without time-consuming manual data review and migration.

claim: A Lifecycle policy can be specified at the prefix level or at the bucket level.
question: At what level is a Lifecycle policy set?

values.display: prefix or at the bucket level

evidence.quote: You can specify the policy at the prefix or at the bucket level.

claim: A Lifecycle rule can, for example, archive all objects under the prefix logs/ to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval 30 days after creation and expire them after 365 days.
question: What does a typical Lifecycle rule look like?

evidence.quote: For example, you could create a rule that archives into S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval all objects with the common prefix “logs/” 30 days from creation and expires these objects after 365 days from creation.
